market_mood: SpaceX's Starlink spectrum push blew a hole in the telecom sector while Middle East risk (Houthi strikes on Riyadh, tanker attacks in Hormuz) keeps jet fuel and shipping in focus, even as Trump's softer Iran tone pushed oil down. Long-end Treasury yields near 24-year highs remain the quiet pressure on everything.
self_check: My oil and energy calls have been my best theme (74%) while AI & tech calls have been poor (25%), so today I leaned on energy/geopolitics and framed tech ideas around overdone one-day moves rather than narrative bets. Bearish calls have held up slightly better than bullish ones, so I let two shorts in.

picks.reason: Crown Castle jumped 13% in a session that crushed the carriers on the SpaceX/Starlink spectrum news; a tower REIT whose tenants are AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile is unlikely to be a long-term winner from a satellite threat to those same customers, and high long-end yields hurt REITs.

T-Mobile fell 13% on the SpaceX spectrum announcement, but it already has a direct-to-cell partnership with Starlink and the satellite threat to mainstream mobile service is years away; the selloff looks like an overreaction that can partly retrace.

Delta cut its full-year profit outlook on a $6 billion jet-fuel hit and is now weighing whether to even launch Riyadh flights after Houthi strikes on the airport; the Middle East fuel and airspace problem keeps compounding.
Gold hit a one-week high with 24-year-high Treasury yields, escalating Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and record tanker attacks in Hormuz all feeding safe-haven demand.

Shares were slammed on the report Starbucks explored a takeover; analysts note the strategic logic given Niccol ran both chains, and the selloff in the target of a deal report is an unusual setup worth watching.

top_buys.pitch: A tower REIT that soared 13% on the same day its carrier tenants were destroyed makes little sense.
top_buys.why: SpaceX announced a spectrum deal to push Starlink deeper into US telecom, sending Verizon, AT&T and T-Mobile down 10-13%. Crown Castle's entire revenue base is leases to those same carriers, so a structural threat to them is not bullish for towers over time. On top of that, 10- and 30-year yields sit at 24-year highs, which is a direct headwind for rate-sensitive REITs. The one-day spike looks like a crowded rotation trade rather than a fundamental repricing.
top_buys.risks: The move may reflect real news I can't see, such as a lease renewal or asset sale, and towers can be bid as a defensive haven if carriers are seen cutting capex elsewhere.
top_buys.watch: Any carrier capex commentary and whether the 30-year Treasury yield keeps rising.

top_buys.pitch: Delta cut guidance on a $6 billion fuel hit and now may not even launch its Riyadh route.
top_buys.why: The airline reduced its full-year earnings outlook because of jet fuel prices driven by the Middle East war. Separately, Houthi strikes killed three people at Riyadh airport and EU aviation regulators widened airspace warnings, putting Delta's Saudi expansion in doubt. Fuel is the single biggest swing factor for airline earnings and the geopolitical source of the problem is escalating, not fading. The cost pressure should keep showing up in estimates over coming weeks.
top_buys.risks: Oil fell on Trump's conciliatory Iran comments; a real de-escalation or diplomatic breakthrough would send airlines sharply higher.
top_buys.watch: Jet fuel crack spreads and whether Delta confirms or cancels the Riyadh launch.

top_buys.pitch: A 13% one-day drop on a satellite headline for the carrier that already partners with Starlink.
top_buys.why: T-Mobile has an existing direct-to-cell deal with Starlink, so SpaceX going deeper into telecom is less of an existential threat to it than to peers. Satellite service remains far from matching terrestrial 5G capacity in cities, and spectrum deployment takes years. A 13% single-session loss in a large-cap, low-beta wireless name is the kind of panic move that often partly retraces.
top_buys.risks: If SpaceX positions Starlink as a direct consumer competitor and cancels or dilutes the T-Mobile partnership, the de-rating could continue.
top_buys.watch: Any detail on SpaceX's spectrum plans and whether the T-Mobile partnership is reaffirmed.

top_buys.pitch: Gold is grinding to new highs on war risk and 24-year-high bond yields.
top_buys.why: Gold hit a one-week high even as oil softened, which suggests demand is being driven by something other than inflation hedging: geopolitical fear and distrust of the long bond. Houthi strikes inside Saudi Arabia and the worst week of Hormuz tanker attacks since the Iran war began are the kind of escalation that keeps safe-haven bids alive. Reuters also flagged four signs the bond market could get uglier, which historically supports hard assets.
top_buys.risks: A genuine Iran diplomatic breakthrough or a sharp drop in yields would take the air out of the gold trade quickly.
top_buys.watch: Headlines on US-Iran talks and the 30-year Treasury auction/yield.

top_buys.pitch: Chipotle shares got hit on takeover chatter rather than bid up, an unusual and potentially correctable reaction.
top_buys.why: The FT reported Starbucks explored a takeover of Chipotle, and the market punished Chipotle on the report. Analysts interviewed argue Brian Niccol, who ran both chains, could actually make it work, which implies real strategic interest in the asset. If a deal never happens, Chipotle still trades on its own improving fundamentals at a lower starting price.
top_buys.risks: The weakness may reflect genuine fears about Chipotle's own traffic trends, and fast-casual demand is soft with consumers complaining about costs.
top_buys.watch: Chipotle's upcoming quarterly results and any formal company comment on the merger report.

summary.watch: Big bank earnings next week and whether long-end Treasury yields keep climbing.
